request_state.conjecture_spec: Beal Conjecture: For positive integers A, B, C, x, y, z with A^x + B^y = C^z and x, y, z >= 3, then gcd(A, B, C) > 1. Strictly requires x,y,z >= 3 (strictly hyperbolic defect 1/x + 1/y + 1/z - 1 <= -1/12). Primitive solutions (gcd(A,B,C)=1) must be non-existent.

candidate_a.title: C614
candidate_a.claim: All primes p in [15701, 15800] with p = 1 mod 3 eliminated via Kraus auxiliary primes q = 2kp + 1 (k <= 18) and trace contradiction against newform 72a1
candidate_a.method: Kraus modular sieve over Frey curve E: Y^2 = X^3 + 2 A X^2 + (A^2 - B^3) X with level 72 / newform 72a1

candidate_b.title: C616
candidate_b.claim: All primes p in [15801, 15900] with p = 1 mod 3 eliminated via Kraus auxiliary primes q = 2kp + 1 (k <= 33) and trace contradiction against newform 72a1
candidate_b.method: Kraus modular sieve over Frey curve E: Y^2 = X^3 + 2 A X^2 + (A^2 - B^3) X with level 72 / newform 72a1

orthogonality.instructions: Are the mathematical mechanisms of Candidate A and Candidate B mathematically orthogonal (e.g. local Galois deformation vs. global Arakelov heights, or bounded modular sieve vs. cyclotomic Selmer descent)?

criteria.true: The two mechanisms operate on independent mathematical structures and can be combined.
criteria.false: The two mechanisms are redundant, parallel, or share the exact same mathematical foundation.

obstruction_compensation.instructions: Does the strength of Candidate A compensate for the primary obstruction of Candidate B? (For example, does Candidate A's local congruence bound the bad reduction set S that obstructs Candidate B?)

criteria.true: Candidate A provides information that strictly removes or weakens Candidate B's obstruction.
criteria.false: Neither candidate resolves the obstruction of the other; the obstructions are compounding.

breakthrough_potential.instructions: Estimate the breakthrough potential of a synthesized hybrid method combining Candidate A and Candidate B.
criteria: level 0: No synergy; synthesis yields no new leverage beyond the individual candidates.
level 1: Minor synergy; provides slightly improved computational bounds or local certificates.
level 2: Strong synergy; closes a major gap for an infinite signature family.
level 3: Definitive breakthrough; creates a viable, unconditional path toward full Beal.

synthesis_action.instructions: What action should be taken on this candidate pair?

criteria.formulate_hybrid_candidate: Formulate a new hybrid candidate combining the two complementary invariants.
criteria.discard_pair: Discard pair; shared failure modes or redundant mechanisms.
criteria.keep_independent: Keep independent; both are valuable but do not synthesize into a unified proof.
